scope: Selected comparison evidence; supplement to the October 1 scoping review, not a new systematic search. National models are not estimates for any listed tour stop.

airQualityBenefitPerMWh.boundary: National modeled air-quality benefits only; excludes climate benefits

sources.authors: Dev Millstein, Eric O’Shaughnessy and Ryan Wiser
sources.title: Climate and air quality benefits of wind and solar generation in the United States from 2019 to 2022
sources.type: Generation/emissions analysis with modeled health benefits
sources.finding: Wind and solar displace fossil generation; avoided harms depend on the counterfactual grid and valuation assumptions.
sources.limit: National historical estimates, not clinical observations or a transferable benefit for each new MWh at any site.

sources.authors: Minghao Qiu, Corwin M. Zigler and Noelle E. Selin
sources.title: Impacts of wind power on air quality, premature mortality, and exposure disparities in the United States
sources.finding: Choosing which generators reduce output can improve health benefits; maximizing total benefits does not automatically close exposure disparities.
sources.limit: Historical generation and theoretical dispatch scenarios, not observed neighborhood disease reductions.

sources.authors: Irene van Kamp and Frits van den Berg
sources.title: Health Effects Related to Wind Turbine Sound: An Update
sources.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 18(17), 9133
sources.finding: Annoyance is the most consistent association. Other health findings are inconsistent or limited.
sources.limit: Wind-turbine evidence does not set data-center noise thresholds or establish equivalent exposure.

sources.title: Wind turbine proximity and health-related quality of life in Germany 2002 to 2022
sources.finding: No robust adverse average effect from turbine presence in the primary specifications; a density analysis found lower mental quality of life.
sources.limit: Proximity is not measured noise; pretrend assessment and multiple specifications limit inference. Not a universal safe distance.

sources.title: The Photovoltaic Heat Island Effect: Larger solar power plants increase local temperatures
sources.type: Field microclimate measurements at an Arizona installation
sources.finding: Measured warmer nighttime air over the PV installation relative to nearby desert.
sources.limit: On-site temperature measurements do not establish heat illness or temperatures in neighboring homes.

sources.title: Four water insecurity concerns about datacenters driving the AI revolution
sources.type: Scholarly essay using public records and literature
sources.finding: Connects water demand with transparency, allocation, household costs and resilience.
sources.limit: Identifies concerns and research needs; does not estimate a causal increase in disease or household insecurity.

sources.authors: Neha Gour, Luis Ortiz and Edward Maibach
sources.title: Health implications of the rapid rise of data centers in Virginia: an exploratory assessment
sources.type: Peer-reviewed mini review; existing core record L23
sources.finding: Describes air, noise, water, land-use and affordability pathways and calls for direct health research.
sources.limit: An exploratory synthesis of scholarly and grey sources, not a resident cohort or measured causal health effect.
